sections.h2: What does the Webster County PVA do, and what does it leave to others?
sections.html:
The Webster County Property Valuation Administrator assesses real and personal property inside the county at fair market value. That is the whole job: the PVA does not decide how much tax you pay. A bill has two parts, the assessed value and the tax rate, and the rate comes from elected bodies such as the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and districts like the library and health boards.

A few categories are valued in Frankfort instead, including public service companies, bank shares, omitted tangible property, and vehicles. The PVA can still adjust a vehicle's value for high mileage or documented repair estimates.

The office is on the first floor of the Webster County Courthouse, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Call 270-639-7016, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. The Sheriff's Office shares the same building address and answers at 270-639-5067, and its website lists a Property Taxes page for bill and payment details.

sections.h2: When must Webster County property taxes be paid?
sections.html:
Webster County follows the statewide collection calendar in KRS 134.015. Full payment by November 1 earns a 2 percent discount, the printed amount is due through December 31, and penalties start on January 1. Ask the Sheriff for the dates printed on your own bill, since the Department of Revenue may move to an alternative schedule when bills are mailed late.

  • Through November 1: pay the bill minus 2 percent.
  • November 2 to December 31: pay the face amount.
  • January: add 5 percent.
  • After January 31: add 10 percent, until the April 15 close of collection.

At the close of business on April 15, every unpaid bill passes from the Sheriff to the County Clerk, who records a lien against the property and adds fees. Payments to the Sheriff stop at that point, and the next stop for a payoff is the Clerk's office, which answers recordings and tax questions at 270-639-7006.

sections.h2: How much more does a delinquent Webster County bill cost?
sections.html:
The jump at April 15 is large, and it keeps growing for as long as the certificate sits at the Clerk. Kentucky's Department of Revenue publishes a worked example for a bill of $1,000, and the Webster County Clerk's office handles delinquent real estate taxes using the same steps.

Cost of a $1,000 tax bill once it reaches the County Clerk (Department of Revenue example)
StageTotal due
Transferred from Sheriff (penalty and add-on included)$1,254.00
Paid within five business days$1,387.79
Paid after the county attorney's first notice$1,611.30
Paid in May, with two months of interest$1,627.61
Paid after the June advertisement$1,659.90
Paid by a third party at the tax sale$1,704.21

The sale cannot be held sooner than 90 days or later than 135 days after the transfer. A buyer at that sale takes over the lien and can add its own fees to what you owe.

sections.h2: How can a Webster County owner dispute an assessment?
sections.html:
The first move is a conference with the PVA or a deputy, which the law requires before any appeal. During it the PVA has to explain the rules and how your value was produced, and a form records the opening value, your claimed value, and the result.

The roll is open to the public for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May. A Webster County owner who talked to the PVA files the appeal at the County Clerk's office by close of business the day after the last inspection day. The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days later and hears evidence only with both sides present.

  • Documents the board expects: physical description of the land and buildings, insurance policies, construction costs, and sales listings of similar property.
  • Paid agents must be attorneys, CPAs, licensed brokers or appraisers, or another recognized professional, and must carry written authorization.
  • You may record the hearing audio.

When bills are printed before the dispute ends, your claimed value is used, and a supplemental bill follows if the board lands higher.

sections.h2: Is there a break for older or disabled Webster County homeowners?
sections.html:
Yes: the homestead exemption. Owners who are 65 or older, or totally disabled under a federal or retirement program, can take $49,100 off the assessed value of the home they live in for 2025 and 2026. The application goes to the PVA, with a birth certificate, driver's license, or passport as proof of age.

Webster County's Census median owner-occupied value is $112,900. After the exemption, the taxable value would be $63,800. At the 2025 state real property rate of 10.6 cents per $100, the state share drops from about $119.67 to about $67.63. County, city, school, and district rates add to that.

For disability, payments must have run for the whole assessment period. Veterans with a service-connected disability and owners found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or Kentucky Retirement Systems keep the exemption without annual reapplication. Anyone else on a disability basis applies again each year.

sections.h2: What does selling a Webster County house with back taxes involve?
sections.html:
The balance follows the property. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and the lien under KRS 134.420 lasts 11 years regardless of who holds title. A buyer's title search will turn it up, so get written payoff figures from both the Sheriff (current year) and the County Clerk (prior years) before you accept an offer.

The Clerk's website offers a delinquent tax lookup alongside land records. If your bill was sold at the tax sale, the payoff goes to the third-party buyer and includes its fees, so ask who holds the certificate.

Current-year tax is usually split in the sale contract between seller and buyer by days of ownership. Put the split in writing and have the closing agent show it on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Webster County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Webster County was formed in 1860 from parts of Henderson, Hopkins, and Union counties and named for Daniel Webster. Dixon is the seat, Providence is the largest city, and Clay, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft complete the six cities. The county lies in the Western Coal Field region and is the southernmost county in the Evansville, Indiana and Kentucky metro area. It keeps Central time.

Census QuickFacts reports:

  • 12,929 residents in 2025, down 0.7 percent from the 2020 base, across 332 square miles of land.
  • 5,772 housing units and 4,923 households.
  • 73.8 percent owner-occupied, median value $112,900.
  • Median household income $59,628; 16.1 percent in poverty.
  • Mean commute of 28.7 minutes, longer than in Washington or Wayne County.
  • Five building permits in 2025.

With so few new homes going up, resale is the main market. Sellers dealing with an inherited property, repairs, or unpaid taxes can sell as-is to a cash buyer and pay off the lien at closing.

faqs.q: Where is the Webster County PVA office?
faqs.a: It is on the first floor of the courthouse at 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon. The phone is 270-639-7016, and hours are Monday through Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m.

faqs.q: Who sets my Webster County property tax rate?
faqs.a: Elected bodies do, such as the fiscal court, city governments, the school board, and library and health districts. The PVA only sets the assessed value.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Webster County assessment?
faqs.a: Confer with the PVA first, then file with the County Clerk by the close of business the day after the roll inspection ends. The inspection period is 13 days starting the first Monday in May.

faqs.q: What is the Webster County homestead exemption for 2026?
faqs.a: It is $49,100 off assessed value for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. You must own and live in the home and be 65 or older, or classified as totally disabled.

faqs.q: How much more will I owe if my Webster County bill goes to the County Clerk?
faqs.a: Expect a 10 percent penalty, a sheriff's add-on, 1 percent monthly interest, and commissions. Revenue's example turns a $1,000 bill into $1,254 at transfer and about $1,611 after the first county attorney notice.
